subject: Geography
central_question: How do climate, soil, altitude and human activity shape India’s vegetation, forests, wildlife and conservation strategies?
in_scope_units: Meaning and regional diversity of natural vegetation.
Evergreen, semi-evergreen, deciduous and thorn forests.
Littoral, swamp and mangrove forests and wetlands.
Forest conservation policy and social forestry.
Wildlife conservation, species projects and biosphere reserves.
banned_topics: Detailed monsoon circulation, which belongs to Climate.
Detailed physiographic divisions, which belong to Structure and Physiography.
Mineral classification and the rock cycle, which belong to Minerals and Rocks.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any planted garden tree is natural vegetation.
known_pitfalls.correction: Natural vegetation is a community left undisturbed long enough to adjust to climate and soil.
They lack one common leaf-shedding season, so the forest remains green.

known_pitfalls.claim: All deciduous forests receive the same rainfall.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter distinguishes moist and dry deciduous types.

known_pitfalls.claim: Social forestry means only village tree planting.
known_pitfalls.correction: It includes urban, rural and farm forestry.

known_pitfalls.claim: A biosphere reserve is identical to a national park.
known_pitfalls.correction: A biosphere reserve is an ecosystem-level area linked with UNESCO’s MAB framework.

recommended_example_progression: Use Exercise 2(i) to define natural vegetation and evergreen conditions.
Use Exercise 2(ii) to explain social forestry.
Use Exercise 2(iii) to define biosphere reserves.
Use Exercise 3(ii) to discuss people’s participation in conservation.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter includes Exercises 1(i–v), 2(i–iv), 3(i–ii), and map and local-plant Project/Activity tasks.
